title: Lesson 4. Grandma's presents
subtitle: too и enough: слишком и достаточно

sections.title: 1. Too and enough
sections.text: {too} + adjective means {more than necessary} (negative): It's {too} beautiful! This dress is a bit {too} short. {not} + adjective + {enough} means {less than necessary} (negative): I'm {not} thin {enough} to wear this dress. Adjective + {enough} means {as much as necessary} (positive): You are old {enough} to wear a tie. {Too} goes {before} the adjective; {enough} goes {after} the adjective. To change a sentence with too: My jeans are {too short} → They are {not long enough}.
chain: not + adj + enough = меньше, чем нужно

sections.title: 2. Granny's presents
sections.text: Granny has bought clothes for Nick and Rosie, but they are not happy. Nick says: I think I have {enough} shirts, Gran. Besides, I am {too} messy. Rosie says: I'm not {thin enough} to wear this lovely dress. Granny says: You are {old enough} to wear a tie. At the end she says: I think I'm {too old-fashioned} to buy clothes for you.
chain: Rosie: not thin enough for the dress
Granny: old enough for a tie

sections.title: 3. The shopping list
sections.text: The list has {vitamins}, {a jar of} marmalade, a {board game}, {a packet of} cereal, a new red {hat}, some {party clothes}, ten {postcards}, some {bread} and {a pair of} shoes. You can buy vitamins at the {chemist's}, marmalade, cereal and bread at a {grocery}, a board game at a {toy shop}, postcards at a {newsagent's} and shoes at a {shoe shop}.

flashcards.a: Больше, чем нужно (негативно): It's too expensive.
Меньше, чем нужно (негативно): I'm not thin enough.
Достаточно (позитивно): You are old enough to wear a tie.

flashcards.a: He / she is not fast enough.

timeline.title: Недостаточно (негатив)
timeline.text: I'm not thin enough to wear this lovely dress. I'm not good enough to wear it.
